notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 1 simply supported 35-ft bay, W36X387 + MC18X42.7 girder, one 40-ton cab crane, on new freestanding W14X342 columns with welded twin-rib bracket seats, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. The flexible plate on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio flange-tie-weld-fatigue 4.68 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X60 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 0.5 in plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 4 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X342 columns against the twist: 0.0230 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.251 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.483 in), still beyond a limit (column-twist or column-twist-rotation fails and stays in the calculation: a stiffer strut, a torsionally stiffer column or a column cap is needed). With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 28.75 in off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.0698 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.761 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.483 in). The strut is sized so the girder's twist movement under the factored traction stays within 0.063 in (a configurator target, tightened from 1/8 in where the tie could not take the movement, so the tie, slots and gaps are not sized by it).

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 115 kip, is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 50 kip for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider column caps over the new columns; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Welded twin-rib seat) is kept and checked here.

The flexible plate on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio flange-tie-weld-fatigue 4.68 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap.

No W and channel cap pair meets every sizing target; the closest: top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 1.67, vertical deflection 0.43 and lateral 0.85 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 836 by cap channel fit, 131 by sizing ratio, 240 by flange width, 1 by AISC F13.2 proportions; the next lighter, W36X395 + C15X33.9: W flange too wide for the channel with the weld pocket and tie room. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios. The closest section is within the limits but not the sizing margins: the calculation decides.

New cantilever column for a 40-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The W14X257 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 1.31 > 0.9: the lightest heavier W14 within the drift and torsion ratios.

fabrication.steel: W girder ASTM A992; cap channel and connection plates ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops. Cap: continuous fillet each W top-flange edge, with the end development shown. Full cap bearing contact required. Bearing stiffeners CJP to the W top flange, bottom fitted.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC. Capped girder shop sequence: weld and UT the bearing stiffener CJPs and any under-flange attachments, check the top flange flatness, then fit and weld the cap.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
